name: Kon Tum food guide
summary: Breakfast is two bowls of phở khô, dry noodles with fermented black soybean sauce and a clear broth beside them. Go Vietnam puts those shops around the market from about 6:00 to 10:00, at about 20,000–33,000 VND, or up to 35,000 VND for a large bowl. Gỏi lá is the leaf platter on Trần Cao Vân. The leaf count and the platter price are not one figure.
body: Eat the morning at the market. One bowl is sun-dried rice noodles tossed with meat and black soybean sauce. The other is hot broth. Alternate them. Then the day can be the leaf salad, or cơm lam and a grilled village chicken if you are out at a Ba Na or Xơ Đăng table. The evening drink is coffee. Vietnam Tourism calls the highland bean Robusta and calls Kon Tum the coffee hub. Go Vietnam’s cluster article calls the town cup arabica. Both stay.
Twenty-four specialties follow, from those publishers. Eight of them belong to Măng Đen, Tu Mơ Rông, or the wider highland pot, not to the market breakfast. Where two prices are in print, both stay.
specialtiesLead: Start with the two bowls. The leaf salad, the bamboo tube, and the jar are the rest of the highland table.

sections.heading: Kon Tum specialties
paragraphs: These are the dishes publishers tie to the city, the market, or the Ba Na and Xơ Đăng table around it. Phở khô is the breakfast. Gỏi lá is the platter on Trần Cao Vân. Cơm lam and grilled chicken travel as a pair, and their prices do not agree. Jar wine is the festival jar, not the morning bowl.

sections.heading: Beyond the market
paragraphs: Măng Đen and Tu Mơ Rông are not the market breakfast. The Măng Đen pig, the sturgeon-head pot, and the bird noodle soup sit on Go Vietnam’s Măng Đen article. The Ngọc Linh salads and the forest greens are the Xơ Đăng festival list at Tu Mơ Rông. Gnetum-leaf soup and the bamboo-tube soup are highland pots Go Vietnam ties to the former Kon Tum area, with city addresses still Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Order phở khô. Go Vietnam says the shops run mainly from about 6:00 to 10:00, around Kon Tum market and the central streets, including Phan Chu Trinh, Phan Đình Phùng, and Tô Hiến Thành. The printed bowl is about 20,000–33,000 VND, or up to 35,000 VND for a large bowl, on that 2025 reference.

sections.heading: Streets
paragraphs: Two eating streets have a publisher. The market is the morning noodles. Trần Cao Vân is the leaf salad. A restaurant name is not part of either line.

spots.name: Kon Tum market
spots.address: Central Kon Tum, around the market
spots.note: Go Vietnam says two-bowl phở is sold around the market and on the central streets, mainly from about 6:00 to 10:00. The bowl on that 2025 reference is about 20,000–33,000 VND, or up to 35,000 VND for a large bowl.

spots.name: Tran Cao Van
spots.address: Trần Cao Vân, Kon Tum city
spots.note: VietnamNet on 23 July 2023 says gỏi lá is especially easy to find on this street, at 100,000–150,000 VND for a platter for about 3–4 people. The Vietnam News Agency prints about 300,000–400,000 VND for a platter for 6–8 people. Go Vietnam’s Măng Đen article prints 350,000–600,000 VND for a platter for 4–6 people. A clock was not printed. Check on arrival.

seoTitle: Kon Tum food guide — two-bowl pho and leaf salad
seoDescription: Dry pho in two bowls from about 6:00 to 10:00, leaf salad on Trần Cao Vân, and bamboo-tube rice with grilled chicken. Where a price disagrees, both figures stay.
